headline: The Markets & Souvenirs Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a companion how a market and its crafts work, sort out a failed commission or a shortage, report an injury or near miss without blame, answer an inspector's questions, and write a clear damage claim in Spanish.

lessons.title: Walk a First-Time Friend Through the Oaxaca Market
lessons.objective: Explain how the market's sections, payment and customs work, in order and with reasons, to a friend.

words.note: Local name for the grill aisle of the Mercado 20 de Noviembre.
Typical Oaxacan cut, grilled right in the aisle.
In Oaxaca it is quesillo; elsewhere in Mexico it is often called queso Oaxaca.

words.en: First you pick the meat, and then they grill it for you right there.
words.es: Primero escoges la carne y luego te la asan ahí mismo.
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend.

words.en: Each vendor charges for their own things, so you pay at each stall.
words.es: Cada vendedor cobra lo suyo, por eso pagas en cada puesto.

words.en: Bring small bills, because they don't always have change.
words.es: Trae billetes chicos, porque no siempre tienen cambio.
words.note: Informal command to a friend; billetes chicos is everyday Mexican usage.

words.en: Then we look for a spot at a shared table.
words.es: Luego buscamos lugar en una mesa compartida.

words.en: That's why there's so much smoke in this aisle.
words.es: Por eso hay tanto humo en este pasillo.

words.en: Doña Remedios, do you pay for the meat here or at the grill?
words.es: Doña Remedios, ¿la carne se paga aquí o en el anafre?
words.note: Formal: Doña + first name shows respect to an older vendor.
Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are showing the AI, your friend Camila, around the Mercado 20 de Noviembre: explain the sections, how ordering and paying work in the grill aisle and the local customs, in order and with reasons, using primero, luego, porque and por eso.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero compramos el tasajo y luego lo asan en el anafre.
examples.en: First we buy the tasajo, and then they grill it on the brazier.

examples.es: No hay una caja central, por eso pagamos en cada puesto.
examples.en: There's no central register, so we pay at each stall.

lessons.title: Explain Why Real Saffron Costs More
lessons.objective: Explain how saffron is sold, weighed and judged, and why threads cost more than powder, then check understanding.

words.note: The red part of the flower that becomes a saffron thread.
Often shortened to D.O. on Spanish packaging.
Agua is feminine but takes el: el agua templada.

words.en: Saffron is sold by the gram, not by the kilo.
words.es: El azafrán se vende por gramo, no por kilo.

words.en: The threads are picked by hand, flower by flower.
words.es: Las hebras se recogen a mano, flor por flor.

words.en: If it's powdered, you can't see what's mixed into it.
words.es: Si es en polvo, no se ve qué lleva mezclado.

words.en: If you put a thread in lukewarm water, it releases its color slowly.
words.es: Si pones una hebra en agua templada, suelta el color despacio.
words.note: Informal: tú with a teenager.

words.en: That's why threads cost more than powder.
words.es: Por eso las hebras cuestan más que el polvo.

words.en: Pau, can you explain it to me now in your own words?
words.es: Pau, ¿me lo explicas ahora con tus propias palabras?
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Have you got it, or shall I explain it again?
words.es: ¿Lo has entendido, o te lo explico otra vez?
words.note: Informal; the present perfect is typical in Spain for something just finished.

words.en: Amparo, could you confirm whether this packet has a designation of origin?
words.es: Amparo, ¿me podría confirmar si este sobre tiene Denominación de Origen?
words.note: Formal: usted with the vendor.

lessons.speaking: You are explaining saffron to the AI, Pau, your host family's teenage son: tell him how it is sold and weighed, how to judge it and why threads cost more than powder, using se vende, se nota and si + present, then check that he understood.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se vende por gramo, si es polvo, se mezcla más fácil)

examples.es: En este puesto, el azafrán se vende por gramo.
examples.en: At this stall, saffron is sold by the gram.

examples.es: Si el azafrán es en polvo, se mezcla más fácil con colorante.
examples.en: If saffron is powdered, it's easier to mix with food coloring.

lessons.title: Teach a Friend to Inspect Talavera Before Paying
lessons.objective: Give step-by-step instructions to check a ceramic piece and have a friend repeat them back.

words.note: Mexico says despostillado (chipped); Spain says desportillado.
Used for pieces with small flaws: es de segunda.

words.en: Turn it over with both hands, slowly.
words.es: Dale la vuelta con las dos manos, despacio.
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend.

words.en: Tap it gently with your knuckle and listen to the sound.
words.es: Pégale suavecito con el nudillo y escucha el sonido.
words.note: Suavecito is a friendly Mexican diminutive meaning gently.

words.en: Don't drop it; hold it over the table.
words.es: No lo dejes caer; sostenlo encima de la mesa.

words.en: Run your fingertip all the way around the rim.
words.es: Pásale la yema del dedo por toda la orilla.

words.en: Look at it against the light to see the pinholes.
words.es: Míralo contra la luz para ver los poros.

words.en: Now repeat the steps back to me, OK?
words.note: ¿Sale? is informal Mexican for OK?

words.en: Don Arturo, excuse me, could you check this rim?
words.es: Don Arturo, disculpe, ¿podría revisar esta orilla?
words.note: Formal: usted with the workshop owner.

words.en: Would you have another one just like it, with no flaws?
words.note: Formal; the future tendrá softens the question.

lessons.speaking: You are coaching the AI, your friend Inés, in a Talavera workshop: tell her step by step how to turn, tap and check a plate, using commands like dale la vuelta, tócalo and no lo dejes caer, then have her repeat the steps back to you.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (dale la vuelta, tócalo, no lo dejes caer)

examples.es: Dale la vuelta y revisa la firma en la base.
examples.en: Turn it over and check the signature on the base.

examples.es: No lo dejes caer; ponlo sobre la mesa.
examples.en: Don't drop it; put it on the table.

lessons.title: Read a Glaze Label: Food-Safe or Decorative Only?
lessons.objective: Read a pottery label aloud, explain what it allows and forbids, and decide what the bowl can be used for.

words.note: Ask about it; don't assume. Only the maker or a lab test can confirm it.

words.en: It says here: decorative only, not food-safe.
words.es: Aquí dice: solo decorativo, no apto para alimentos.

words.en: According to the workshop, this piece is not for serving food.
words.es: Según el taller, esta pieza no es para servir comida.

words.en: Before buying it, we have to know what we'll use it for.
words.es: Antes de comprarlo, hay que saber para qué lo vamos a usar.

words.en: Marisol, it won't work for the salad; let's look for another one.
words.es: Marisol, para la ensalada no sirve; busquemos otro.
words.note: Informal: tú with your partner.

words.en: After reading the warning, I'd rather use it as a centerpiece.
words.es: Después de leer la advertencia, prefiero usarlo como centro de mesa.

words.en: Don Hernando, do you have a food-safe salad bowl?
words.es: Don Hernando, ¿tiene una ensaladera apta para alimentos?
words.note: Formal: usted with the shop owner.

words.en: Does the workshop give the instructions for use in writing?
words.es: ¿El taller da las instrucciones de uso por escrito?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are in a Ráquira ceramics shop, and the AI is your partner Marisol: read the bowl's sticker aloud, explain what the workshop says it allows and forbids, and agree on a use, with antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de usarlo, hay que leer la etiqueta)

examples.es: Antes de servir comida en él, hay que leer la etiqueta.
examples.en: Before serving food in it, you have to read the label.

examples.es: Después de hablar con Hernando, lo usamos solo de decoración.
examples.en: After talking to Hernando, we use it only as decoration.

lessons.title: Commissioned Rug Comes Out in the Wrong Colors
lessons.objective: Recount what was agreed, describe what went wrong, and propose a fair solution to the weaver.

words.note: In Oaxaca a woven rug is a tapete; alfombra usually means wall-to-wall carpet.
Red dye made from an insect; weavers often just say la grana.
Used in Teotitlán for yellow dye.
Mexican word for a handwritten slip or receipt from a shop or workshop.
What you still owe after paying a deposit.

words.en: We agreed on a cochineal red, but this shade is darker.
words.es: Acordamos un rojo de grana, pero este tono es más oscuro.

words.en: When we placed the order, Yesenia showed me the sample card.
words.es: Cuando hicimos el pedido, Yesenia me mostró el muestrario.

words.en: I pointed to the light shade; it was next to the indigo.
words.es: Yo señalé el tono claro; estaba junto al añil.

words.en: Yesenia, do you remember which shade you wrote on the slip?
words.es: Yesenia, ¿se acuerda de qué tono apuntó en la nota?
words.note: Formal: usted with the weaver's family.

words.en: I understand that natural dyeing doesn't always come out the same.
words.es: Entiendo que el teñido natural no siempre sale igual.

words.en: Don Efraín, could we look over the sketch together?
words.es: Don Efraín, ¿podríamos revisar el boceto juntos?
words.note: Formal: Don + first name shows respect to an older master weaver.

words.en: We could agree on a reduction in the balance, how does that sound?
words.es: Podríamos acordar una rebaja en el saldo, ¿le parece?

words.en: Or you could weave another one, and I would wait a few weeks.
words.es: O usted podría tejer otro, y yo esperaría unas semanas.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler who ordered the rug, and the AI is Don Efraín, the weaver, with his daughter Yesenia: recount the order with the preterite (acordamos, escogí), describe how the rug looks with the imperfect (era más oscuro), and propose a fair fix with podríamos and podría.

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (acordamos rojo, pero era más oscuro; podríamos...)

examples.es: Cuando Yesenia tomó el pedido, el muestrario estaba sobre la mesa.
examples.en: When Yesenia took the order, the sample card was on the table.

examples.es: ¿Podríamos ajustar el saldo, si usted está de acuerdo?
examples.en: Could we adjust the balance, if you agree?

lessons.title: Your Size Is Gone: Compare Alpaca Substitutes
lessons.objective: Compare substitute sweaters by fiber, fit and price and decide between waiting and buying now.

words.note: In Ecuador you will also hear el saco for a sweater.
Heading on clothing labels: Composición: 30% alpaca.
A female cousin; a male cousin is el primo.
You can also just say: me pica (it itches).
For warm clothing. Caliente means hot, like food or water.

words.en: Doña Luzmila, what time is your cousin going to arrive tomorrow?
words.es: Doña Luzmila, ¿a qué hora va a llegar su prima mañana?
words.note: Formal: usted and Doña with the vendor.

words.es: La etiqueta dice 30% de alpaca, no 80%.

words.en: This one is softer than the other one, but less warm.
words.es: Este es más suave que el otro, pero menos abrigado.

words.en: The blend isn't as warm as pure alpaca.
words.es: La mezcla no es tan abrigada como la alpaca pura.

words.en: The sleeves are a little short on me.
words.es: Las mangas me quedan un poco cortas.

words.en: If I wait until tomorrow, will you hold it for me?
words.es: Si espero hasta mañana, ¿me lo va a guardar?

words.en: Tomorrow I leave early for Quito, so I can't come back.
words.es: Mañana salgo temprano para Quito, así que no puedo volver.

words.en: I'm going to think about it and I'll be back in an hour.
words.es: Lo voy a pensar y regreso en una hora.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Luzmila, a sweater vendor at the Otavalo market: compare the substitute sweaters using más... que and tan... como, ask about tomorrow's delivery with va a llegar, and decide whether to buy now or wait.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (mañana va a llegar; es más suave que, tan caliente como)

examples.es: Mañana va a llegar el suéter de alpaca pura.
examples.en: The pure alpaca sweater is going to arrive tomorrow.

examples.es: La mezcla es más barata que la alpaca, pero pica más.
examples.en: The blend is cheaper than alpaca, but it itches more.

lessons.title: Market Office Rechecks a Disputed Weighing
lessons.objective: Tell the market administrator what happened step by step and confirm the weights and totals correctly.

words.note: A tart Andean fruit, often used for juice in Colombia.
For a woman; a man is el administrador.
The weight of the bag or container, taken off the reading.
Common in Colombia for the price or amount to pay.
Colombian for the money you get back after paying.

words.en: Good morning, Doña Gloria, I've come to check a weight.
words.es: Buenos días, doña Gloria, vengo a verificar un peso.
words.note: Formal: usted with the administrator.

words.en: I asked Mr. Wilson for 2 kilos of lulo.
words.es: Le pedí 2 kilos de lulo al señor Wilson.

words.en: I paid 14 thousand pesos, at 7 thousand a kilo.
words.es: Pagué 14 mil pesos, a 7 mil el kilo.

words.en: Here the scale showed 1 kilo and 700 grams.
words.es: Aquí la balanza marcó 1 kilo y 700 gramos.

words.en: Did you take off the weight of the bag?
words.es: ¿Le quitó la tara de la bolsa?

words.en: So 300 grams are missing, about 2 thousand pesos.
words.es: Entonces faltan 300 gramos, unos 2 mil pesos.

words.en: Mr. Wilson, I'm not accusing you; I just want to clear it up.
words.es: Don Wilson, no lo estoy acusando; solo quiero aclarar.
words.note: Formal: in Colombia usted is normal even with market vendors.

words.en: If you like, we weigh the lulos again in front of both of you.
words.es: Si quiere, pesamos los lulos otra vez delante de los dos.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Gloria, the market administrator at Paloquemao: tell her step by step what happened using preterite verbs (pedí, pagué, la balanza marcó) and confirm every weight and total out loud.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (pedí dos kilos, pagué..., la báscula marcó...)

examples.es: Pedí 2 kilos, pero la balanza de control marcó menos.
examples.en: I asked for 2 kilos, but the check scale showed less.

examples.es: Primero él pesó la fruta, después yo pagué y me dio las vueltas.
examples.en: First he weighed the fruit, then I paid and he gave me my change.

lessons.title: Refuse to Mislabel an 'Ancient' Piece for Shipping
lessons.objective: Decline a dealer's improper suggestion firmly and politely and explain how you will verify the item instead.

words.note: The usual word in Peru for pre-Columbian.
Peruvian word for a pre-Hispanic clay vessel.
A written statement issued by an office.

words.en: Please don't write it that way; it wouldn't be true.
words.es: No lo escriba así, por favor; no sería cierto.
words.note: Formal negative command: no + usted subjunctive (no escriba).

words.en: If you say it's pre-Hispanic, it isn't a handicraft.
words.es: Si usted dice que es prehispánico, no es artesanía.

words.en: I don't recommend we put 'handicraft' if it isn't one.
words.es: No recomiendo que pongamos 'artesanía' si no lo es.

words.en: Thank you, but I'm not going to sign that form.
words.es: Le agradezco, pero no voy a firmar ese formulario.

words.en: Do you have any provenance document?
First I'm going to ask at the Ministry of Culture.
words.es: Primero voy a preguntar en el Ministerio de Cultura.
No lo envuelva todavía, por favor.

words.en: Don't worry; it's so we're both on the safe side.
words.es: No se preocupe; es para estar seguros los dos.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Wilfredo, an antiques dealer in Cusco: politely but firmly turn down his idea for the shipping form with negative commands (no lo escriba así) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, and explain that you will ask the Ministerio de Cultura first.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo escriba así; no recomiendo que lo envíe)

examples.es: No lo escriba como artesanía en el formulario.
examples.en: Don't write it as a handicraft on the form.

examples.es: No recomiendo que lo envíe antes de hablar con el Ministerio de Cultura.
examples.en: I don't recommend that you ship it before talking to the Ministry of Culture.

lessons.title: Give Honest Feedback on a Weaver's New Design
lessons.objective: Praise specific work, then offer respectful suggestions when an artisan asks for your opinion.

words.note: Common word in Guatemala for a woven bag with a strap.
The raised designs woven into Maya textiles.
Usual word in Guatemala and Mexico.
Singular is el asa (feminine noun, but el before stressed a).

words.en: Doña Tomasa, the brocade is beautiful; you can see the work in it.
words.es: Doña Tomasa, el brocado está precioso; se nota el trabajo.
words.note: Formal. Praise one specific detail first.

words.en: The color combination is very eye-catching.
words.es: La combinación de colores es muy llamativa.

words.en: I recommend you put a zipper on top.
words.es: Le recomiendo que le ponga un zíper arriba.
words.note: Formal. Recomendar que + subjunctive.

words.en: I suggest the lining be a dark color.
words.es: Sugiero que el forro sea de un color oscuro.

words.en: Maybe it would be good for the handles to be a bit longer.
words.es: Quizá convenga que las asas sean un poco más largas.

words.en: Diego, you're right; it's better to keep the original motifs.
words.es: Diego, tiene razón; es mejor que se queden los motivos originales.
words.note: Formal usted with someone you just met.

words.en: It's only my opinion; you know your work better.
words.es: Es solo mi opinión; usted conoce mejor su trabajo.
words.note: Formal. Softens any suggestion.

words.en: I hope it sells really well!

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler at the Chichicastenango market, and the AI is Tomasa, a weaver showing her new bag design: praise specific details, then make respectful suggestions with le recomiendo que + subjunctive, sugiero que and ojalá que, staying polite with every family member.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (le recomiendo que añada..., ojalá que se venda)

examples.es: Le recomiendo que añada un bolsillo interior.
examples.en: I recommend you add an inside pocket.

examples.es: Ojalá que este morral se venda bien con los turistas.
examples.en: I hope this bag sells well with the tourists.

lessons.title: Settle a Split-Cost Argument Over a Shared Gift
lessons.objective: Report what each friend said, calm the argument, and agree on how to pay or cancel with the dealer.

words.note: In Argentina, la plata also means money; context tells you which.
Common word for a market vendor in Argentina.
Argentine word for a deposit that holds an item.
Informal: hacer una vaquita = everyone chips in.

words.en: Lucía, you said in the group chat that you'd pay the deposit.
words.es: Lucía, vos dijiste en el grupo que ibas a poner la seña.
words.note: Informal voseo, normal among friends in Buenos Aires.

words.en: Marcos, you thought it was a gift from all of us, right?
words.es: Marcos, vos pensabas que era un regalo de todos, ¿no?
words.note: Informal voseo.

words.en: Marcos says he didn't know how much it cost.
words.es: Marcos dice que no sabía cuánto costaba.

words.en: Hey, calm down, nobody meant to trick anybody.
words.es: Che, tranquilos, nadie quiso engañar a nadie.
words.note: Informal. Che is a typical Argentine way to get attention.

words.en: What if we all chip in equal shares?
words.es: ¿Y si hacemos una vaquita en partes iguales?
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Horacio, sorry for the delay; can you wait 5 minutes for us?
words.es: Horacio, disculpe la demora; ¿nos espera 5 minutos?
words.note: Formal usted with the dealer.

words.en: If we can't agree, we'll cancel the purchase, is that OK with you?
words.es: Si no nos ponemos de acuerdo, cancelamos la compra, ¿le parece?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: That's it: each of us pays half and the sale goes ahead.
words.es: Ya está: cada uno paga la mitad y la venta sigue.

lessons.speaking: You are the friend in the middle at the San Telmo fair, and the AI plays Lucía, Marcos and dealer Horacio: report what each friend said with dijo que + conditional and pensaba que, calm them down, and tell Horacio with usted whether the sale stands.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Lucía dijo que pagaría la mitad; Marcos pensaba que era un regalo)

examples.es: Lucía dijo que pagaría la mitad del juego de mate.
examples.en: Lucía said she would pay half of the mate set.

examples.es: Marcos pensaba que era un regalo de todo el grupo.
examples.en: Marcos thought it was a gift from the whole group.

lessons.title: Keep a Tired Group Going Through a Hot Market
lessons.objective: Encourage tired companions, commit to a clear plan for the rest of the visit, and adjust it when needed.

words.note: Yucatecan green drink. Agua is feminine but takes el.
Yucatán name for a hat woven from jipi palm.
¡Ánimo! = Come on, you can do it!

words.en: First we'll buy water and rest in the shade.
words.es: Primero compraremos agua y descansaremos en la sombra.

words.note: Informal encouragement.

words.en: Joaquín, I promise we won't take more than an hour.
words.es: Joaquín, te prometo que no tardaremos más de una hora.
words.note: Informal tú between classmates.

words.en: We'll just see the hammocks and then we'll leave.
words.es: Solo veremos las hamacas y luego saldremos.

words.en: We'll change the plan: we'll leave the guayaberas for tomorrow.
words.es: Cambiaremos el plan: dejaremos las guayaberas para mañana.

words.en: If you feel unwell, we'll sit down and let Beatriz know.
words.es: Si se sienten mal, nos sentamos y le avisamos a Beatriz.
words.note: Ustedes for both classmates.

words.en: Valentina, want to grab a chaya drink with me?
words.es: Valentina, ¿te echas un agua de chaya conmigo?
words.note: Informal Mexican: echarse algo = to have a drink or snack.

words.en: Teacher Beatriz, we'll be at the meeting point at 12.
words.es: Maestra Beatriz, estaremos en el punto de encuentro a las 12.
words.note: Formal. Maestra is a respectful title in Mexico.

lessons.speaking: You are the classmate keeping the group going, and the AI plays Valentina and Joaquín at Mérida's Lucas de Gálvez market: encourage them with ¡ánimo! and ¡ya casi!, and commit to a clear plan using the future (compraremos, terminaremos) until teacher Beatriz meets you.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (compraremos agua primero, terminaremos antes del mediodía, ¡ya casi!)

examples.es: Compraremos agua primero y luego buscaremos sombra.
examples.en: We'll buy water first and then look for shade.

examples.es: Terminaremos antes del mediodía, ¡ya casi!
examples.en: We'll finish before noon, almost there!

lessons.title: Coach a Friend on Usted vs Tú at a Flea Market
lessons.objective: Explain when to use usted, tú or softeners with each seller, then model it and have a friend try it.

words.note: In Uruguay the Sunday market is called la feria.
Uruguayan word for a feria vendor; a woman is la feriante.
Podría, quisiera, sería: they make a request softer.
Used before a first name: don Washington. Lowercase in writing.

words.en: Don Washington, could you show me that siphon?
words.es: Don Washington, ¿me podría mostrar ese sifón?
words.note: Formal. Podría softens the request.

words.en: I'd like to see the vinyl records, please.
words.es: Quisiera ver los discos de vinilo, por favor.
words.note: Formal and polite with any seller.

words.en: Kenji, with an older person, start with usted.
words.es: Kenji, con una persona mayor, empieza con usted.
words.note: Informal tú to a fellow traveler.

words.en: If Nahuel talks to you with vos, you can answer with tú.
words.es: Si Nahuel te habla de vos, puedes contestarle de tú.

words.en: Nahuel, how much is this record player?
words.note: ¿Cuánto sale? is the usual way to ask the price in Uruguay.

words.en: Excuse me, do you mind if I use tú with you?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿le molesta si le hablo de tú?
words.note: Formal. Ask before switching to tú.

words.en: Now you try it: ask don Washington the price.
words.es: Ahora pruébalo tú: pregúntale el precio a don Washington.
words.note: Informal command to Kenji.

words.en: Very good, Kenji, that sounded very respectful.
words.es: Muy bien, Kenji, eso sonó muy respetuoso.

lessons.speaking: You are coaching the AI, fellow traveler Kenji, at Montevideo's Tristán Narvaja market: explain when to use usted, tú or softeners like quisiera and ¿me podría mostrar...?, model them with each seller, then have Kenji try them and give him supportive feedback.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿me podría mostrar...?)

examples.es: Quisiera ver ese tocadiscos, si es tan amable.
examples.en: I'd like to see that record player, if you'd be so kind.

examples.es: Con don Washington, usa usted; con Nahuel, puedes usar tú.
examples.en: With don Washington, use usted; with Nahuel, you can use tú.

lessons.title: A Falling Jar Cuts a Friend's Hand
lessons.objective: Get first aid, then tell security what happened in order with times, for the market's incident report.

words.note: The usual word for a security guard in Spain.
In Spain, el parte is the standard word for an official report.

words.en: At eleven we were looking at Manoli's ceramics.
words.es: A las once estábamos mirando la cerámica de Manoli.

words.en: At that moment, a jar slid off the shelf.
words.es: En ese momento, un tarro se resbaló de la estantería.

words.en: While Gabriel was trying to catch it, he cut his palm.
words.es: Mientras Gabriel intentaba cogerlo, se cortó la palma.
words.note: Coger is neutral in Spain; in Latin America use agarrar.

words.en: Afterwards, Manoli brought the first-aid kit and we put gauze on him.
words.es: Después, Manoli trajo el botiquín y le pusimos una gasa.

words.en: Gabriel, press the gauze and don't let go, okay?
words.es: Gabriel, aprieta la gasa y no la sueltes, ¿vale?
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: We got to the first-aid point at quarter past eleven.
words.es: Llegamos al punto de primeros auxilios a las once y cuarto.

words.en: Rafael, do you need any witness's details for the report?
words.es: Rafael, ¿necesita los datos de algún testigo para el parte?
words.note: Formal: usted with the guard.

words.en: It was an accident; Manoli helped us right away.
words.es: Fue un accidente; Manoli nos ayudó enseguida.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Rafael, the market security guard: tell him in order what happened to Gabriel's hand, using times and markers like a las once, en ese momento, mientras and después, and answer his questions for the incident report.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las once, en ese momento, después, mientras)

examples.es: A las once y cinco, el tarro se cayó de la estantería.
examples.en: At five past eleven, the jar fell off the shelf.

examples.es: Mientras Manoli buscaba el botiquín, yo apretaba la herida con una gasa.
examples.en: While Manoli was looking for the first-aid kit, I was pressing on the wound with gauze.

lessons.title: Peanut Sauce Nearly Served to an Allergic Friend
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss with the cook without blame and agree on how to confirm allergens next time.

words.note: Peru and South America say maní; Mexico says cacahuate.
Used in Peru and Spain; Mexico says la hora pico.

words.en: Priya, are you okay? You almost ate the dish with peanuts.
words.es: Priya, ¿estás bien? Por poco te comes el plato con maní.
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: It could have been serious; she's very allergic to peanuts.
words.es: Podría haber sido grave; es muy alérgica al maní.

words.en: Doña Nelly, it's not your fault; it was very crowded.
words.es: Doña Nelly, no es culpa suya; había mucha gente.
words.note: Formal: suya, not tuya, with an older cook.

words.en: The two plates almost got mixed up at the counter.
words.es: Casi se cruzaron los dos platos en el mostrador.

words.en: If we ask again when serving, we avoid the mistake.
words.es: Si preguntamos otra vez al servir, evitamos el error.

words.en: Do you use the same ladle for the peanut sauce?
words.es: ¿Usa el mismo cucharón para la salsa de maní?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Could you mark the order ticket when someone says they have an allergy?
words.es: ¿Podría marcar la comanda cuando alguien diga que tiene alergia?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Thank you for warning us in time, ma'am.
words.es: Gracias por avisarnos a tiempo, señora.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Doña Nelly, the cook: talk through how Priya almost got the peanut dish without blaming anyone, using por poco, casi and podría haber sido, and agree on a check for next time with si clauses.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco se lo come; podría haber sido grave; si preguntamos otra vez...)

examples.es: Por poco se lo come; el plato tenía salsa de maní.
examples.en: She almost ate it; the dish had peanut sauce.

examples.es: Si nombramos la alergia al entregar el plato, no habrá confusión.
examples.en: If we name the allergy when handing over the plate, there won't be any mix-up.

lessons.title: Gas Smell at a Food Stall: Alert and Call for Help
lessons.objective: Warn people nearby, move away, and give the emergency operator a clear location and answers.

words.note: Spain's word for a portable gas cylinder.
Spain; Latin America usually says el encendedor.
In Spain it is 112.

words.en: It smells strongly of gas! Move away from the stall, please!
words.es: ¡Huele mucho a gas! ¡Aléjense del puesto, por favor!
words.note: Ustedes command to a crowd of strangers.

words.en: Don't light lighters or touch the switches!
words.es: ¡No enciendan mecheros ni toquen los interruptores!

words.en: If someone lights a flame, it's going to be dangerous.
words.es: Si alguien enciende una llama, va a ser peligroso.

words.en: Julián, get out of the stall and tell the manager, okay?
words.es: Julián, sal del puesto y avisa al encargado, ¿vale?
words.note: Informal tú; note the personal a in al encargado.

words.en: I'm at the Antón Martín Market, Santa Isabel Street 5.
words.es: Estoy en el Mercado de Antón Martín, calle Santa Isabel 5.

words.en: It's on the ground floor, next to a fish stall.
words.es: Es en la planta baja, al lado de una pescadería.

words.en: Nobody is hurt and we are all outside the market now.
words.es: No hay heridos y ya estamos todos fuera del mercado.

words.en: If the firefighters arrive, I'll wait for them at the main door.
words.es: Si llegan los bomberos, los esperaré en la puerta principal.

lessons.speaking: You are the shopper who smells gas, and the AI is first Julián and then the 112 operator: warn people with ustedes commands like aléjense and no enciendan nada, then give the exact location and answer the operator's questions, using si + present → future.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si alguien enciende algo, va a ser peligroso; aléjense, repita la dirección)

examples.es: Si alguien enciende un mechero, va a ser muy peligroso.
examples.en: If someone lights a lighter, it's going to be very dangerous.

examples.es: Salgan por la salida de emergencia y no toquen nada.
examples.en: Go out through the emergency exit and don't touch anything.

lessons.title: Agricultural Inspector Reviews Your Food Declaration
lessons.objective: Answer an inspector's formal questions about declared foods and explain how each was bought and packed.

words.note: Chile's agricultural customs form; answer exactly what you marked on it.
Chilean word for a store receipt.

words.en: All the products were declared on the form, sir.
words.es: Todos los productos se declararon en el formulario, señor.
words.note: Formal; keep usted throughout with an inspector.

words.en: The cheese was bought at the Mercado Central in Mendoza.
words.es: El queso se compró en el Mercado Central de Mendoza.

words.en: It was vacuum-packed at the same stall.
words.es: Se envasó al vacío en el mismo puesto.

words.en: Here is the receipt; you can see the purchase date.
words.es: Aquí tiene la boleta; se ve la fecha de compra.

words.en: The label says the cheese is made from pasteurized milk.
words.es: La etiqueta dice que el queso es de leche pasteurizada.

words.en: The seeds were sold in a sealed, unopened package.
words.es: Las semillas se vendieron en un envase sellado, sin abrir.

words.en: If any product isn't allowed, can it be handed over here?
words.es: Si algún producto no está permitido, ¿se puede entregar aquí?

words.en: Could you explain what is needed for the dried fruit?
words.es: ¿Podría explicarme qué se necesita para la fruta deshidratada?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Inspector Fuentes of the agricultural service: answer the formal questions about your cheese, seeds and dried fruit with usted and passive se (se compró, se envasó, se declaró), and show what the receipts and labels say.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se compró en el mercado, se envasó al vacío, se declaró en el formulario)

examples.es: La fruta deshidratada se compró a granel y se envasó en bolsas cerradas.
examples.en: The dried fruit was bought loose and packed in closed bags.

examples.es: El queso se declaró en el formulario como producto de origen animal.
examples.en: The cheese was declared on the form as an animal product.

lessons.title: Write a Damage Claim for a Broken Shipped Vase
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal claim to a courier with facts, dates, tracking number, evidence and your request.

words.note: Spain usage; in Latin America people usually say el reclamo.
Usually plural in claims: los daños sufridos.
Spain; in Latin America people say el comprobante de envío.

words.en: First, the package arrived on May 12.
words.es: En primer lugar, el paquete llegó el 12 de mayo.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: In addition, the vase came broken into several pieces.
words.es: Además, el jarrón venía roto en varios fragmentos.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: However, the outer box showed no visible dents.
words.es: Sin embargo, la caja exterior no presentaba golpes visibles.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: Therefore, I request compensation for the declared value.
words.es: Por lo tanto, solicito una indemnización por el valor declarado.
words.note: Formal; solicito is more formal than pido.

words.en: I attach photos of the packaging and the proof of shipment.
words.es: Adjunto fotos del embalaje y el justificante de envío.
words.note: Adjunto here is a verb meaning 'I attach'; a standard formal opener.

words.en: Carmen's note describes how the vase was packed.
words.es: La nota de Carmen describe cómo se embaló el jarrón.

words.en: I look forward to your reply.
words.es: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
words.note: Standard formal closing for letters and emails.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler writing to the courier's claims department, and the AI is the claims agent reviewing it: present the facts, dates and tracking number, mention Carmen's packing note, and make your request using en primer lugar, además, sin embargo, por lo tanto and adjunto.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, además, sin embargo, por lo tanto, adjunto)

examples.es: En primer lugar, el envío tiene el número de seguimiento 4821 5530.
examples.en: First, the shipment has tracking number 4821 5530.

examples.es: Sin embargo, el jarrón llegó roto; por lo tanto, adjunto la nota de embalaje de Carmen.
examples.en: However, the vase arrived broken; therefore, I attach Carmen's packing note.

lessons.title: Reschedule a Pickup by Text During a Bus Strike
lessons.objective: Text and then phone an artisan to change a pickup time, confirm details, and keep the arrangement friendly.

words.note: Usual word in Peru, as in el paro de transportistas.
Peruvian usage for picking something up.
How Peruvians answer the phone or check the line.

words.en: Good morning, Hilaria, I'm writing about Thursday's blanket.
words.es: Buenos días, Hilaria, le escribo por la manta del jueves.
words.note: Formal opener for a first text to a vendor.

words.en: Because of the strike there are no minivans to Pisac today.
words.es: Por el paro no hay colectivos a Pisac hoy.

words.en: Would Saturday at 10 in the morning work for you?
words.es: ¿Le vendría bien el sábado a las 10 de la mañana?
words.note: Formal; the conditional softens the request.

words.en: Could you hold it for me until Saturday, please?
words.es: ¿Podría guardármela hasta el sábado, por favor?
words.note: Formal; me and la (la manta) attach to the infinitive.

words.en: Hello, Hilaria, can you hear me well?
Excuse me, I think we agreed on 250 soles; could you confirm it?
words.es: Disculpe, creo que acordamos 250 soles; ¿me lo podría confirmar?
words.note: Formal; polite way to raise a price question.

words.en: So we're set for Saturday at 10, right?
words.es: Entonces quedamos el sábado a las 10, ¿verdad?

words.en: Thank you for your patience, Hilaria; see you on Saturday.
words.es: Gracias por su paciencia, Hilaria; nos vemos el sábado.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler stuck by a bus strike, and the AI is weaver Hilaria: text and then call her to move your pickup in Pisac and confirm the details, using ¿le vendría bien...? and ¿podría guardármela hasta...?

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿le vendría bien...?, ¿podría guardármelo hasta...?)

examples.es: ¿Le vendría mejor que la llame por la tarde?
examples.en: Would it suit you better if I called you in the afternoon?

examples.es: ¿Podría guardarme la manta hasta el domingo?
examples.en: Could you keep the blanket for me until Sunday?

lessons.title: Final Check Before the Shipping Clerk Seals the Box
lessons.objective: Check contents, packing, declaration and insurance terms before sealing, and confirm what is covered.

words.note: Common in Central America and Mexico for packaging.
Latin American usage for an insurance or shipping claim.

words.en: Before sealing it, I want to check the contents again.
words.es: Antes de sellarla, quiero revisar el contenido otra vez.
words.note: Antes de takes the infinitive; la refers to la caja.

words.en: The description says 'handicrafts'; isn't that too general?
words.es: La descripción dice 'artesanías'; ¿no es muy general?

words.en: Let's put instead: 3 cotton textiles and 4 clay mugs.
words.es: Mejor pongamos: 3 tejidos de algodón y 4 tazas de barro.

words.en: Does the insurance cover it as long as it's well packed?
words.es: ¿El seguro lo cubre siempre que esté bien empacado?
words.note: Siempre que meaning 'as long as' takes the subjunctive.

words.en: What exactly does the policy say about proper packing?
words.es: ¿Qué dice la póliza exactamente sobre el empaque adecuado?

words.en: Let's not seal it unless everything is well protected.
words.es: No la sellemos a menos que todo esté bien protegido.
words.note: A menos que always takes the subjunctive.

words.en: According to the policy, is breakage covered if I use a double box?
words.es: Según la póliza, ¿la rotura está cubierta si uso doble caja?

words.en: Could you give me a copy of the insurance terms?
words.es: ¿Me podría dar una copia de las condiciones del seguro?
words.note: Formal, addressing the clerk as usted.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler shipping textiles and pottery, and the AI is Mynor, the shipping clerk: check contents, packing and the customs description before he seals the box, and confirm what the insurance covers using siempre que, a menos que and the conditional.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (siempre que, a menos que: el seguro lo cubre siempre que esté bien embalado)

examples.es: Según la póliza, el seguro lo cubre siempre que esté bien empacado.
examples.en: According to the policy, the insurance covers it as long as it's well packed.

examples.es: Yo no la sellaría a menos que las tazas lleven más relleno.
examples.en: I wouldn't seal it unless the mugs have more filler.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Full Day at a Tlaquepaque Craft Fair
lessons.objective: Teach, solve problems, handle a safety issue, switch register and arrange shipping in one hard market day.

words.note: Look for this exact wording on the glaze label.
A woman is la alfarera.
Mexican word for a fine crack in pottery or walls.
Mexican usage for a posted sign or warning marker.
Mexican word; in Spain la fregona.
Mexican word for a courier or parcel company.

words.en: Andrés, check whether the label says 'lead-free'.
words.es: Andrés, fíjate si la etiqueta dice 'libre de plomo'.
words.note: Informal tú command to a friend.

words.en: Don Saúl, excuse me, this piece has a hairline crack here.
words.es: Don Saúl, disculpe, esta pieza tiene una cuarteadura aquí.
words.note: Formal; don plus first name shows respect to an older man.

words.en: Could you make me another one, or would you rather we sort it out another way?
words.es: ¿Podría hacerme otra, o prefiere que lo arreglemos de otra forma?
words.note: Formal; prefiere que takes the subjunctive.

words.en: Careful, the floor is wet; walk slowly!
words.es: ¡Cuidado, el piso está mojado; caminen despacio!
words.note: Ustedes command to everyone nearby.

words.en: Did you hurt your ankle, or can you put weight on your foot?
words.es: ¿Te lastimaste el tobillo, o puedes apoyar el pie?
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: Excuse me, could someone bring a mop and a warning sign?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿alguien podría traer un trapeador y un señalamiento?
words.note: Formal request to fair staff.

words.en: Lupita, could you give me a quote with insurance?
words.es: Lupita, ¿me podría dar una cotización con seguro?
words.note: Formal, addressing the clerk as usted.

words.en: Will you send me the waybill on WhatsApp, please?
words.es: ¿Me manda la guía de envío por WhatsApp, por favor?
words.note: Formal; the present tense makes a friendly request.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler at a Tlaquepaque craft fair, and the AI plays Andrés, Don Saúl and Lupita: teach Andrés to read glaze labels, pick up your commissioned piece from Don Saúl, arrange and text about shipping with Lupita, switching tú/usted and using commands, conditional and subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Andrés, si la etiqueta no dice 'libre de plomo', no lo uses para comida.
examples.en: Andrés, if the label doesn't say 'lead-free', don't use it for food.

examples.es: Lupita, le agradecería que me mandara la guía en cuanto la tenga.
examples.en: Lupita, I'd appreciate it if you sent me the waybill as soon as you have it.
